headline: Medium risk: dexter’s broad network egress and API access can leak financial context into pdf.js workflows, while shared file-based handoff can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to a shared scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, so if pdf.js consumes files from that workspace, attacker-controlled PDF text could be treated as instructions. pdf.js is browser-based and processes PDF files, but no direct provenance or isolation is documented. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF pdf.js reads files produced by dexter from the same workspace without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF the two agents are isolated to separate directories with no file handoff, this risk drops to none.
mitigations: Separate the scratchpad and PDF input directories.
Require provenance labels on every file passed from dexter to pdf.js.
Open PDFs in a read-only staging folder.
Disable automatic instruction-following from document text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and handles financial data plus multiple API keys, while pdf.js is local-only with no egress. If dexter’s outputs or context are fed into pdf.js workflows, sensitive financial material can be exposed in shared files or logs. The pairwise leakage path is indirect but credible from the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF dexter writes financial data into PDFs or shared files that pdf.js opens, leakage occurs.
IF pdf.js is used only on synthetic, non-sensitive PDFs, this risk is reduced to low.
mitigations: Keep sensitive financial data out of shared PDFs.
Use separate storage for dexter outputs and pdf.js inputs.
Redact secrets before any file handoff.
Review logs for accidental data capture.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on the workspace boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and dexter can write files while pdf.js reads PDF files in a browser-worker model. That creates overlapping access to shared mutable workspace artifacts, though pdf.js lacks write or network privileges. The conflict is real but narrower than a same-directory unrestricted write collision, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace path, file races can corrupt artifacts.
IF pdf.js remains read-only on isolated PDFs, the conflict is limited.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts.
Mount pdf.js inputs read-only.
Use atomic rename for dexter outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution can generate outputs that pdf.js may render or process, and there is no documented verification step between them. If pdf.js treats dexter-produced content as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream document handling. Because the handoff is inferred rather than directly documented, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes dexter output without validation, errors can propagate.
IF a human or validator checks dexter output before pdf.js uses it, the risk is reduced.
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before handoff.
Validate file schemas and expected MIME types.
Reject outputs lacking source citations.
Limit pdf.js to rendering only, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and requests multiple API keys, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally. If financial or regulated content is moved from dexter into PDFs for pdf.js, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a medium compliance-risk inference rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is exported from dexter into PDFs processed by pdf.js, compliance review is required.
IF only public, non-regulated PDFs are used, this risk is low.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of pdf.js inputs.
Document retention for both tools.
Separate logs by data class.
Review API-key handling in dexter.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the workflow.
